name: Garage Door Repair
lead: Most garage door problems are a single worn component, not a door that needs replacing. We diagnose the actual fault and fix it, usually in one visit.
signs: Door reverses partway, or refuses to close at all
Grinding, banging or scraping during travel
Door hangs crooked or binds against the track
Opener runs but the door does not move
detail: We are a repair-only shop. Because we do not sell new doors, there is never a reason for us to tell you a door is beyond saving when it is not. A technician inspects springs, cables, rollers, hinges, tracks and the opener, explains what failed and what it costs, and completes the work with parts carried on the truck.

name: Garage Door Maintenance
lead: An annual service visit is the difference between replacing a $12 roller and replacing a bent panel. Most emergency calls we take were preventable.
signs: The door has not been serviced in over a year
It has become noticeably louder
Rollers or hinges look dry or rusted
The door drifts when stopped halfway
detail: Maintenance covers lubricating moving parts, tightening hardware that vibrates loose over thousands of cycles, balancing the door against the spring, adjusting travel and force limits on the opener, and testing the photo-eye and auto-reverse safety features. You get a written note of anything wearing out so nothing is a surprise later.

name: Garage Door Spring Repair
lead: A broken torsion spring is the single most common garage door failure, and the most dangerous one to attempt yourself. Springs hold hundreds of pounds of stored energy.
signs: A loud bang from the garage, then the door will not lift
A visible gap in the spring above the door
The opener strains, or lifts a few inches and stops
The door feels extremely heavy by hand
detail: We stock colour-coded torsion springs across the full gauge range on the truck, so a broken spring is almost always same-day. Springs are replaced in pairs where both are the same age, because a second break shortly after the first is otherwise near certain. Do not attempt this repair with hardware-store winding bars.

name: Garage Door Cable Repair
lead: Cables carry the door's weight alongside the springs. A frayed cable is a warning; a snapped one drops the door out of level and can pull it off the track.
signs: One side of the door sits lower than the other
Cable is loose, slack or hanging off the drum
Visible fraying or kinking near the bottom bracket
The door jams diagonally in the opening
detail: Cable repair is fast and inexpensive on its own. Left alone, it turns into bent tracks, damaged panels and a door that has to come off entirely to be rethreaded. If you can see a frayed cable, stop using the door and call us.

name: Garage Door Roller Repair
lead: Worn rollers are the usual reason a door that used to be quiet has become loud enough to hear from inside the house.
signs: Rattling or scraping as the door travels
The door shudders instead of gliding
Rollers look chipped, flat-spotted or seized
Metal dust along the track
detail: We replace worn steel rollers with nylon rollers, which run quieter and do not need constant lubrication. A full set is a short visit and makes an immediate, obvious difference to how the door sounds and feels.

name: Garage Door Hinge Repair
lead: Hinges take the flex every time the door bends around the curve of the track. Cracked hinges let panels shift, which is how panel damage starts.
signs: Visible cracks or elongated holes at a hinge
A panel edge that no longer lines up
Popping sounds as the door rounds the curve
Loose or missing hinge screws
detail: Hinges are numbered by position on the door. We carry the common sizes on the truck and replace the failed hinge along with any fasteners that have pulled out of the panel, so the repair holds rather than reopening in a month.

name: Garage Door Track Repair
lead: A bent or misaligned track is why a door jams, grinds, or comes off its rollers mid-travel. It's rarely the track itself that's worn out -- usually something hit it.
signs: Door grinds, sticks or jams partway through travel
A visible bend, dent or gap in the track
Rollers popping out of the track
Door sits crooked or off-level in the opening
detail: Most bent tracks come from a vehicle bump or a roller that failed and let the door bind. We straighten minor bends on site and replace sections that are creased or torn rather than the full track, re-aligning against the door and checking rollers and hinges at the same time so the same failure doesn't repeat.

name: Emergency Garage Door Repair
lead: A garage door stuck open is a security problem, and a door stuck closed can trap a vehicle you need. We answer the phone 24/7.
signs: Door will not close and the garage is left open
Door is off its track or hanging
A spring or cable let go with the door up
Vehicle is trapped inside
detail: Call (604) 240-0180 any hour. We will tell you honestly on the phone whether it is safe to keep operating the door, whether it can wait until morning, and what the visit will involve, before anyone is dispatched.

name: Garage Door Panel and Section Repair
lead: A single damaged section usually does not mean a new door. In most cases the affected panel can be repaired or replaced on its own.
signs: A dented or cracked section after a bump
A panel bowing outward
Separation between sections
Rot or delamination on a wood door
detail: We assess whether the section can be straightened and reinforced or needs replacing, and check the hinges and struts around it, since panel damage is frequently a symptom of a hinge or track problem rather than the cause.

name: Garage Door Remotes and Clickers
lead: A remote that stopped working is often a battery or a lost pairing rather than a failed opener. We sort it out on the spot.
signs: Remote works only from very close range
One remote works and another does not
Remote stopped after a power outage
You need extra or replacement remotes
detail: We are LiftMaster specialists and carry LiftMaster remotes on the truck, including the 992LM and 6580LM. We will also program a remote to a vehicle's built-in HomeLink buttons while we are there.

name: Garage Door Keypads
lead: A wireless keypad means the family gets in without carrying a remote, and you can hand out a code instead of a key.
signs: Keypad no longer responds to the code
Faded or worn keys
Keypad was never installed
You need to change a code someone else knows
detail: We install and program LiftMaster keypads including the 979LM and 387LM, and will show you how to change the code yourself and how to set a temporary code for a house-sitter or contractor.

name: Garage Door Bottom Weather Strips
lead: The bottom seal is what keeps rain, leaves and rodents out of the garage. In this climate it is the part that fails soonest.
signs: Water tracking under the closed door
Daylight visible along the bottom edge
Rubber is cracked, hardened or torn
Draft or debris blowing in
detail: We carry bottom rubber for wood, Steel-Craft and NWD doors and cut it to your opening. If the concrete has settled and left an uneven gap, we will tell you that a thicker seal is the fix rather than replacing the same part again next year.
